newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia aims to speed shipping firm sale - report.
newsitem.headline: Latvia aims to speed shipping firm sale - report.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) wants to speed up the sale of the Latvian Shipping company, one of the largest companies in Latvia, newspaper Bizness I Baltiya on Monday quoted the LPA's head as saying.
Latvian Shipping is estimated to be the world's 19th largest shipping firm and has 39 tankers, 24 reefers (refrigerated vessel) and seven dry cargo vessels. Annual turnover is close to $300 million.

"Now we are beginning talks with those who declared an interest in the privatisation and we simply have to accelerate this process," LPA director-general Janis Naglis told the newspaper in an interview.

Around 14 companies and institutions including Nomura and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) have said they are interested in taking part in the sale of a 25 percent to 35 percent stake in Latvian Shipping.
Naglis said that the company had to confirm its 1997 budget as quickly as possible as this was vital to value the company.
The company is estimated to have a made a loss of $25 million last year and $51 million the year before.
The firm's president Peteris Avotinsh was on Friday dismissed over the losses by the company's council, a body which includes representatives of political parties.
Naglis also said that the agency would sell the company without splitting it into separate operations.
